ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagram shows one large rectangle. A horizontal line divides it into a top row and a bottom row. The top row is divided by two vertical lines into three congruent upright rectangles. The bottom row is divided by one vertical line into two congruent horizontal rectangles. Thus the five smaller rectangles are congruent, with the top three rotated relative to the bottom two. Reasoning: Let each small rectangle have short side x and long side y. From the diagram, the full width of the large rectangle is three short sides across the top, so it is 3x. The same full width is two long sides across the bottom, so it is 2y. Therefore 3x = 2y. The full height of the large rectangle is the long side of a top rectangle plus the short side of a bottom rectangle, so the height is y + x. The large rectangle has perimeter 176, so 2(3x + (x + y)) = 176. This gives 2(4x + y) = 176, so 4x + y = 88. From 3x = 2y, y = 3x/2. Substitute: 4x + 3x/2 = 88, so 11x/2 = 88, giving x = 16. Then y = 24. The perimeter of one small rectangle is 2(x + y) = 2(16 + 24) = 80.

method.method_draft: Use the outer width as the main variable instead of naming the small rectangle sides. Let the large rectangle's width be W.
